newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westfield Trust plans note issue.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westfield Trust plans note issue.

text.p: Retail property trust Westfield Trust, managed by Westfield Holdings Ltd, said on Tuesday it planned a A$250 million convertible note issue at an equivalent price of A$2.40 per unit.
Westfield Trust said the funds would be used for its expansion and redevelopment programme.
It said the world's second largest pension fund, the Dutch-based public sector group ABP, would invest A$150 million to mark its first investment in Australia.
The remaining A$100 million would be invested by another major European-based pension fund, which it did not identify.

Westfield said the total investment would initially consist of A$62.5 million, or 25 percent, with the remaining A$187.5 million to be paid in December 1998 when the notes would convert to 104.2 million Westfield Trust units.

The ABP manager responsible for property investment in the United States and Asia Pacific, Joan Klijnen, said this was ABP's first investment in Australia and followed intensive research. "The calibre of Westfield's management was a major influence in deciding to invest in Westfield Trust, as well as its portfolio of high quality shopping centres," he said.
Klijnen said ABP was already a major investor in Westfield's U.S. operations. The raising was arranged by Dutch-owned investment bank ABN-Amro Hoare Govett.
